Question: What was the story of the outlaw Henry Starr who died in 1921?
Answer: Henry Starr was regarded as the last outlaw from the era of the Old West. He was born on 2nd December 1873 in Fort Gibson, Indian Territory. During his childhood, Henry lost his father and his mother soon remarried. The stepfather was called C.N. Walker and young Henry disliked him from the start. At the beginning of his criminal career, he began by robbing banks. In 1893, Henry was put on trial for the murder of U.S. Deputy Marshal Floyd Wilson. Twice, he was sentenced to hang. On both occasions, the sentence was reduced to imprisonment for manslaughter. Eventually, the outlaw was granted a presidential pardon. Thereafter, Henry formed his own gang and they terrorized parts of Arkansas. A $5,000 reward was placed on his head. Then in 1921, Henry Starr attempted to rob a bank singlehanded in Harrison, Arkansas. He was stopped in his tracks by the bank president - who shot the outlaw with a .38 calibre rifle. The outlaw succumbed to his injuries. Thanks for reading.
